## About these materials

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Citation statement
Please cite these materials as: Von Grebmer zu Wolfsthurn, S., Middleton, S., Ihle, M., & Schönbrodt, F. (2026). *Concept planning for Open Research events* [Quarto slides]. LMU Open Science Center. [https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/concept-planning/](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/concept-planning/)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to **provide future open research instructors and train-the-trainers** with practical skills for **planning and organizing teaching events** on Open Research topics. Through a mix of theoretical elements and hands-on exercises, we will explore **practical considerations** for planning an Open Research event, and discover how to **effectively design and structure** a teaching event so that learners have time to arrive and orient themselves, **reactivate** prior knowledge, get familiar and **process new content** and **obtain feedback** on their learning progress. In this, we will also learn how to **boost motivation** in your learners and how to provide **constructive feedback**.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Aspiring open research instructors**
- **Future open research train-the-trainers** and **educators** in higher education (e.g., universities, colleges) and
- **Self-learners** 

with familiarity about open research challenges, issues and tools and basic didactic skills. 

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Link/Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| Familiarity with Open Science concepts and practices | Examples: Replication crisis, open access, R, version control, preregistration, etc.| [Click here to get familiar with Open Research first](https://lmu-osc.github.io/training/self-learning.html) |
| Didactic principles | A firm grasp on didactic tools for teaching | [Click here to get familiar with didactic principles](https://lmu-osc.github.io/train-the-trainer-open-research/teaching-open-research/core-didactic-principles/) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you will be able to ...

- **Consider** practical and logistical challenges of organizing an Open Research event
- **Structure** an Open Research event according to the five phases of the ARIPE+ scheme [@stadeli2013aviva] to facilitate the learning process
- **Apply** techniques to **enhance** motivation in your learners
- **Understand** key elements of constructive feedback
